title: BME (CDRI-08) mitigates hypoxia-induced hippocampal neurodegeneration and memory impairment via modulating NMDAR-CREB-BDNF signaling and apoptosis reduction
task: Mitigate hypoxia-induced hippocampal neurodegeneration and memory impairment
key_results: BME restored NR2A/NR2B balance, increased CREB-BDNF signaling, reduced cleaved caspase-3 and pro-apoptotic proteins (BAD, BAX), increased Bcl-2 expression, and restored spatial and recognition memory in CoCl2-hypoxia mice
comments: The study demonstrates comprehensive neuroprotection across multiple pathways, though the relative contribution of each signaling axis to the overall therapeutic effect remains unclear.

model_io.model: CoCl2-induced hypoxia mouse hippocampus
outputs: apoptotic markers (cleaved caspase-3, BAD, BAX, Bcl-2, cytochrome C)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hypoxia-induced GluN2B activation and NR2A downregulation with PSD-95 dysregulation initiates apoptotic cascades
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BME restored NR2A/NR2B balance and reduced apoptotic signaling

hypotheses.hypothesis: CREB-BDNF signaling suppression mediates synaptic dysfunction and memory deficits under hypoxia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; BME reversed CREB-BDNF suppression and restored memory function

hypotheses.hypothesis: BME prevents neuronal apoptosis by modulating pro- and anti-apoptotic protein expression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; decreased caspase-3, BAD, BAX, Cyt C and increased Bcl-2

title: Hierarchical grouped convolution and multi-scale vision transformer for uncertainty-aware early breast cancer detection using mammography
task: Uncertainty-aware breast cancer detection from mammography
key_results: 98.67% accuracy, 0.9914 AUC, 14.35% improvement over baseline ViT (84.32%)
comments: Combines hierarchical grouped convolution with multi-scale ViT and calibrated uncertainty estimation; clinically-relevant confidence quantification is valuable but external validation beyond CBIS-DDSM is needed.

model_io.model: HGCViT-UAC (hierarchical grouped convolution + multi-scale vision transformer + Monte Carlo Dropout)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-scale hierarchical feature learning with adaptive attention fusion improves lesion characterization
hypotheses.result: 14.35% accuracy gain over single-scale ViT baseline

hypotheses.hypothesis: Monte Carlo Dropout with calibration provides reliable uncertainty estimates for clinical use
hypotheses.result: 0.019 Expected Calibration Error, 0.026 Brier Score

title: Computational aesthetics for digital interpretation of traditional art and cultural heritage: a two-level benchmark using AVA and heritage image datasets
task: Transfer learning of aesthetic representations from general photographs to cultural heritage images
key_results: ResNet50, EfficientNet B3, ViT, Swin Transformer, and CLIP ViT B/32 evaluated on multi-task aesthetic learning with domain adaptation
comments: Two-level framework with fusion module and explainability (Grad CAM, attention rollout) is methodologically sound, but quantitative performance metrics on heritage datasets are not reported in abstract.

model_io.model: ResNet50, EfficientNet B3, ViT B/16, Swin T, CLIP ViT B/32 with aesthetic-aware fusion module

hypotheses.hypothesis: Aesthetic representations learned from general photography transfer to heritage image domains
hypotheses.result: Framework demonstrates transferability across four heritage datasets via feature freezing and fine-tuning

title: A hybrid 3D-CNN and CGAN approach for bipolar disorder diagnosis using VBM and SBC features from multimodal MRI
task: Bipolar disorder classification from multimodal sMRI and fMRI using 3D-CNN and CGAN augmentation
key_results: 93.49% mean accuracy, 0.97 AUC on cross-validation; 93.02% accuracy, 96.77% specificity on held-out test set; 3.02% accuracy gain from CGAN augmentation
comments: Feature-space augmentation on training data only is methodologically rigorous, but small sample size (49 BD, 121 controls) and lack of multi-site external validation limit clinical generalizability claims.

model_io.model: Dual-branch 3D-CNN with CGAN feature-space augmentation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multimodal integration of structural and functional features outperforms single-modality approaches
hypotheses.result: Multimodal model 93.49% vs. sMRI-only 81.39% and fMRI-only 88.37%

hypotheses.hypothesis: CGAN-based feature augmentation improves classification robustness
hypotheses.result: Mean accuracy gain of 3.02% (95% CI: 1.86–4.19%) across cross-validation runs

title: Design efficiency overcomes scale in reducing AI hallucinations
task: Understanding factors in language model reliability beyond scale
key_results: Non-scale factors account for ~25% of performance variation; 3B-parameter models can match 7B predecessors through design optimization; one-quarter of adversarial prompts defeat all models regardless of scale
comments: Important findings challenging the 'bigger is better' paradigm, though the 25% attribution requires careful interpretation given potential confounding between design and data quality.

model_io.model: Seven language models (1B–7B parameters)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model size alone does not determine reliability; architectural design and training data quality are equally important
hypotheses.result: Design factors explain ~25% of variance; 3B optimized models match 7B baselines

hypotheses.hypothesis: Some fundamental reasoning tasks remain unsolved regardless of scale or architecture
hypotheses.result: ~25% of adversarial prompts defeat all tested models; multi-step reasoning universally problematic

title: Machine learning for intelligent beam divergence compensation in orbital angular momentum-based wireless communication systems
task: Beam divergence compensation in OAM wireless using machine learning
key_results: DNN predicts beamforming weights, achieving 96.2% of optimal received power with latency reduced from 100 ms to 0.5 ms (200× speedup)
comments: Strong practical results for 6G systems; however, evaluation primarily on simulated channels—real-world validation and comparison to adaptive baselines would strengthen claims.

model_io.model: Deep Neural Network for hybrid beamforming weight prediction
outputs: Optimal beamforming weights for OAM beam divergence compensation

hypotheses.hypothesis: ML-learned beamforming weights match iterative optimization while reducing latency by 200×
hypotheses.result: 96.2% of optimal power achieved at 0.5 ms latency vs. 100 ms for traditional methods

title: Energy-efficient and secure federated learning framework for wireless sensor networks in smart agriculture applications
task: Energy-efficient secure federated learning for smart agriculture WSNs
key_results: Energy-efficient and secure FL framework with lightweight encryption; energy-aware node selection improves network lifetime
comments: Well-motivated application but abstract lacks specific quantitative results (energy savings %, convergence speed, accuracy metrics).

model_io.model: Federated Learning with lightweight encryption and energy-aware node selection
inputs: WSN sensor data (crop monitoring, irrigation, environmental)
outputs: Local model updates, aggregated global model, encrypted transmissions

hypotheses.hypothesis: FL with energy-aware node selection and encryption improves energy efficiency, privacy, and convergence
hypotheses.result: Superior performance in energy efficiency, convergence speed, and data protection demonstrated (quantitative metrics not stated in abstract)

title: Analysis of metaheuristic‑optimized ann for predicting surface strip footing bearing capacity in layered cohesionless soils using limit equilibrium analysis
task: Bearing capacity prediction for tapered footing in layered soils
key_results: Test correlation 0.9834 (BBO-MLP), RMSE 130.19 kPa; SHAP identifies footing width as dominant predictor
comments: Solid hybrid approach with explainability; the comparison of four metaheuristics is thorough but differences are incremental.

model_io.model: BBO-MLP, LCA-MLP, SO-MLP, WO-MLP (four hybrid MLP configurations)
inputs: Footing width, upper-layer thickness, friction angles (2,304 limit-equilibrium cases)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Biogeography-based optimization outperforms other metaheuristics for MLP training on geotechnical data
hypotheses.result: BBO-MLP achieved test R² 0.9834, best among four optimizers

title: Application of artificial neural networks for prediction modeling and analysis of the thermophysical properties of Fe₃O₄/water ferrofluid using experimental measurement
task: Artificial neural network prediction of Fe₃O₄/water ferrofluid thermophysical properties
key_results: ANN model achieved R²=0.98 and error 1.56×10⁻⁵ for thermal conductivity; thermal conductivity increased with nanoparticle volume fraction (0.05%–4%), viscosity increased with fraction but decreased with temperature
comments: Solid empirical application; ANN architecture details sparse, and single-model validation without comparison to other regression methods.

model_io.model: Artificial Neural Network for ferrofluid property prediction

hypotheses.hypothesis: ANN can accurately predict ferrofluid thermal conductivity and viscosity from concentration and temperature
hypotheses.result: Thermal conductivity R²=0.98, error 1.56×10⁻⁵; property trends validated experimentally

title: Incorporating hydrometeorological drivers into regime-switching volatility framework for water-level prediction
task: Regime-switching volatility framework for water-level forecasting with hydrometeorological drivers
key_results: MS-gjr-GARCH with ARIMAX exogenous drivers best captured heavy-tailed water-level fluctuations and improved probabilistic forecasting; structural breakpoints significantly influence volatility
comments: Principled integration of multiple time-series techniques; emphasis on hidden states and exogenous drivers is appropriate for hydrology.

model_io.model: ARIMAX-MS-GARCH (sGARCH, eGARCH, gjr-GARCH variants)
inputs: Water-level time series, structural breakpoints, rainfall, API (antecedent precipitation index)
outputs: Conditional mean and variance (regime-dependent), probabilistic water-level forecast

hypotheses.hypothesis: Regime-switching GARCH with exogenous hydrometeorological drivers improves probabilistic forecast accuracy for non-stationary water levels
hypotheses.result: MS-gjr-GARCH achieved best performance; structural changes and exogenous variables substantially influenced model dynamics

title: A preliminary study of ConvMixer in the audio domain using Mel-spectrogram representation for lightweight speech command recognition
task: ConvMixer for speech command recognition using Mel-spectrograms
key_results: ConvMixer-256/8 achieved 96.75±0.11% test accuracy and 0.9675±0.0011 macro-F1 on Vietnamese speech commands (13 classes, 4,460 samples) with 0.72M parameters
comments: Early systematic adaptation of ConvMixer to audio; controlled benchmark protocol ensures fair comparison with ResNet-18, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet, AST; practical for edge deployment.

model_io.model: ConvMixer-256/8 (and baselines: ResNet-18, MobileNetV2, EfficientNet, AST-tiny)
inputs: Mel-spectrograms (128×32) from Vietnamese speech command dataset

hypotheses.hypothesis: ConvMixer remains parameter-efficient and competitive for speech command recognition vs. CNN and Transformer baselines
hypotheses.result: 96.75% accuracy with 0.72M parameters, outperforming ResNet-18 and MobileNetV2 in efficiency-accuracy trade-off

title: Robust hybrid internal model control based smith predictor for MIMO systems with multiple time delays
task: Robust internal model control with Smith predictor for MIMO systems with time delays
key_results: IMC-SP (linear MIMO): 57% settling time reduction, 97% overshoot reduction, 58% tracking error reduction vs. conventional IMC; IMMC-SP (nonlinear): 64% settling time reduction, 70% tracking error reduction vs. decentralized PI; robust to ±50% delay perturbations
comments: Comprehensive extension of classical control theory to nonlinear MIMO; robustness analysis thorough, though simulation-only validation limits practical impact.

model_io.model: IMC-based Smith Predictor (linear and nonlinear MIMO variants)
inputs: MIMO process model with multiple time delays, setpoint references, disturbances
outputs: Control law, manipulated variables, tracking error

hypotheses.hypothesis: IMC-SP structure unifies Smith predictor and IMC advantages, improving setpoint tracking and robustness in MIMO systems with delays
hypotheses.result: 57% settling time reduction (linear), 64% reduction (nonlinear); maintains performance under ±50% delay uncertainty

title: Shear capacity of tapered web panel of plate girders with web opening
task: Shear capacity of tapered web panel in plate girders with openings
key_results: 115 FE models validated against 7 tested girders; EC3-aligned mechanics-based equation developed; capacity sensitive to panel aspect ratio, opening ratio, web slenderness (negative) and tapering angle (beneficial)
comments: Rigorous finite-element study linking experiment, simulation, and design; practical equation useful for engineers, though nonlinear regression fitting limits theoretical insight.

model_io.model: Shell finite-element model (calibrated against 7 tested tapered girders)
inputs: Tapering angle, opening size/shape, panel aspect ratio, web slenderness, footing geometry

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tapering angle, web opening, and slenderness interact nonlinearly in tapered girder web shear capacity
hypotheses.result: FE models reproduced experimental response; EC3-aligned equation captures tapering benefit within investigated range

title: Hybrid classifier for water quality classification from satellite image trained with modified multi texton features
task: Water quality classification from satellite imagery using hybrid deep learning
key_results: ECA-MSNet + LeNet hybrid achieved 96.385% sensitivity; multiple feature modalities (raw, entropy, VI, deep, modified MT) fused
comments: High sensitivity reported but lacks precision, F1, and specificity; averaging two dissimilar architectures is non-standard and results lack statistical rigor.

model_io.model: ECA-MSNet + LeNet hybrid classifier
inputs: Satellite images, preprocessing data, fused features (VI, deep learning, modified multi-texton)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fusion of multiple feature types and hybrid classifier ensemble improves water quality detection
hypotheses.result: ECA-MSNet + LeNet achieved 96.385% sensitivity at TD=90%

title: Analytical solution to the Kronig–Penney model with harmonic oscillator wells: insights to tight-binding
task: Analytical solution to Kronig-Penney model with harmonic oscillator potentials
key_results: Derived energy dispersion, wave functions, and tight-binding tunneling amplitude for harmonic-well version; connections to tight-binding approximation established
comments: Pure theoretical contribution offering modest realism improvement over square wells; practical impact limited as harmonic potentials are still simplified.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Kronig-Penney model with harmonic oscillator wells yields analytical solution with direct tight-binding connection
hypotheses.result: Energy dispersion and wave functions derived; tunneling amplitude expressed in terms of potential parameters

title: Wavelet-based subdomain-enhanced multi-source domain adaptive network for bearing fault diagnosis
task: Multi-source domain adaptive bearing fault diagnosis with wavelet-based features
key_results: Efficient inter-domain alignment and robust fault diagnosis across load and speed variations; fewer parameters and better training efficiency than baselines
comments: Solid engineering of wavelet + multi-source domain adaptation; claims lack specific quantitative metrics (accuracy, AUC) on standard datasets.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-scale wavelet features + private enhancement resolve source conflict and enable robust cross-domain diagnosis

title: Earthquake magnitude estimation using an optimized CNN-DNN-GRU model with binary differential evolution and firefly algorithm

key_results: CNN-DNN-GRU with BDE feature selection + FA hyperparameter tuning: MSE 0.0109, RMSE 0.1048, MAE 0.0837, R² 0.9918 on 3.5M seismic events (1990–2023); supports future early-warning systems
comments: Comprehensive deep learning architecture for large-scale geophysical data; architecture fusion is standard but results are impressive; real-time early warning validation pending.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid CNN-DNN-GRU with metaheuristic optimization achieves high-precision magnitude estimation for early-warning integration

title: Designing female-specific food delivery electric vehicles: a participatory and data-driven approach
task: Female-specific delivery electric vehicle design requirements via participatory research
key_results: Structural equation model identified five latent dimensions (applicability, safety, convenience, friendliness, attractiveness); applicability and safety largest effects on satisfaction
comments: Rigorous qualitative-to-quantitative pipeline with grounded theory and SEM; important for inclusive design but results are descriptive rather than predictive.

model_io.model: Structural Equation Model (SEM) of satisfaction drivers
inputs: Semi-structured interview data (18 riders), survey responses
outputs: Latent dimension estimates, standardized effects on satisfaction, design priorities

hypotheses.hypothesis: Applicability and safety are primary drivers of female rider satisfaction with delivery EVs
hypotheses.result: SEM standardized effects showed applicability and safety largest, followed by convenience, friendliness, attractiveness

title: Prediction-based sign placement using QA sampling
task: Pedestrian flow forecasting and sign placement using quantum annealing as sampler
key_results: SQA reproduces empirical patterns; hardware QA exhibits ~95% constraint violations despite zero chain breaks; classical parallel tempering achieves <1% violations with comparable RMSE
comments: Rigorous comparison revealing fundamental hardware limitations (dynamic range) not connectivity; important cautionary finding for quantum applications, though the practical value remains limited.

model_io.model: QUBO-formulated pedestrian trajectory sampling (SQA, D-Wave hardware, classical parallel tempering)
inputs: Sparse crowd density measurements, transition preferences from headcounts
outputs: Trajectory ensemble, flow forecasts, sign placement recommendations

hypotheses.hypothesis: QUBO sampling produces coherent flow structures consistent with physical constraints and transition preferences
hypotheses.result: SQA valid; hardware QA violates constraints ~95%, destroying coherent flow despite matching marginal RMSE; classical sampler succeeds
